title: SCH-CNT-002 shared elite modifier profile
description: The shared elite modifier profile. The project-owned typed validator in src/MechaMiner.Content/Categories/ remains authoritative; this schema is the draft 2020-12 mirror kept for editor and tool interoperability, and a fixture corpus proves the two reach the same accept/reject verdict on every structural case. See content/schemas/README.md. This is not an enemy and does not validate against the enemy schema: it is a modifier profile applied on top of one, and it shares six fields with an enemy out of sixteen.

id.title: A stable, case-sensitive ASCII content ID

maximum_hull_multiplier.description: How an elite's maximum Hull is scaled.

exclusiveMinimum.derivation: the section makes durations nonnegative and rates non-negative; this quantity is additionally one the definition divides by, scales by, or spends, so zero is excluded as well and the bound is exclusive rather than inclusive

movement_speed_multiplier.description: How an elite's movement speed is scaled.

exclusiveMinimum.derivation: the section makes durations nonnegative and rates non-negative; this quantity is additionally one the definition divides by, scales by, or spends, so zero is excluded as well and the bound is exclusive rather than inclusive

contact_damage_multiplier.description: How an elite's contact damage is scaled.

exclusiveMinimum.derivation: the section makes durations nonnegative and rates non-negative; this quantity is additionally one the definition divides by, scales by, or spends, so zero is excluded as well and the bound is exclusive rather than inclusive

body_scale_multiplier.description: How an elite's body scale is scaled, on top of the enemy's own. The name is the same as the enemy's on purpose: doc 40 requires one name in every scope, and the composition chain reads in one vocabulary because of it.

exclusiveMinimum.derivation: the section makes durations nonnegative and rates non-negative; this quantity is additionally one the definition divides by, scales by, or spends, so zero is excluded as well and the bound is exclusive rather than inclusive

added_control_resistance_percent.description: Percentage points of control resistance an elite gains.

minimum.derivation: the section scopes _percent to human-readable percentage points; the floor of a share of a whole is zero of them, which is the share that is none of it

maximum.derivation: the section scopes _percent to human-readable percentage points; the ceiling of a share of a whole is one hundred of them, which is the whole, and a larger value is not a share of anything

control_resistance_maximum_percent.description: The ceiling an elite's control resistance may reach after the addition. Two bounds live here, so each carries the qualifier that says which it is.

minimum.derivation: the section scopes _percent to human-readable percentage points; the floor of a share of a whole is zero of them, which is the share that is none of it

maximum.derivation: the section scopes _percent to human-readable percentage points; the ceiling of a share of a whole is one hundred of them, which is the whole, and a larger value is not a share of anything

post_hard_control_immunity_seconds.description: An elite's immunity after a hard control effect resolves.

minimum.derivation: the section states that durations are nonnegative and that rates cannot be negative, so the floor of every duration and rate is zero and there is no upper bound the section supplies

adds_behavior.description: Whether the profile adds a behavior.

adds_attacks_phases_aura_or_support_ai.description: Whether the profile adds attacks, phases, an aura, or support AI.

retains_base_identity_behavior.description: What the elite keeps from its base enemy.

maximum_scheduled_elites_at_once.description: How many scheduled elites may be alive at once.

minimum.derivation: the section makes integer currency and rank values integral in source; a count of things that exist begins at one, because a count of zero is the absence of the field rather than a value of it

beacon_elites_additional.description: How beacon elites add to the scheduled ceiling.

modifier_application_order.description: The order in which modifier layers apply. Every layer appears exactly once, so this is a total order over the closed vocabulary rather than a subset of it.

minItems.derivation: the four layers are the whole accepted vocabulary and the field is their total order, so the floor is the vocabulary's size; a shorter array would leave a layer's position undefined

maxItems.derivation: the same vocabulary size as the floor; a longer array would have to repeat a layer, and a total order names each element exactly once

recycling.title: How elites are recycled
recycling.description: Two rules with no structured twin.

presentation_requirements.title: What an elite must show
presentation_requirements.description: Readability requirements for the elite treatment.

insufficient.description: What is explicitly not enough on its own.

version.title: A positive integer version
version.description: The initial schema_version and content_version of every first-authored definition is 1.

minimum.derivation: the initial value of every first-authored definition is 1 and both versions only ever increment, so no valid version is below 1; there is no upper bound because a definition may be revised without limit

name_key.title: Localization key for the player-facing name

summary_key.title: Localization key for the concise player-facing summary

tags.title: Closed query and tooling vocabulary
tags.description: The vocabulary starts empty, so [] is the only accepted value.

presentation_id.title: Logical presentation entry
presentation_id.description: Omitted when a definition never appears in-world. No accepted document mints a grammar for a presentation ID, and inventing one for a category with zero members would be structure ahead of need, so the only constraint is that an authored value is not the empty string.

minLength.rationale: not a capacity bound: the empty string is what the compiler materializes for an omitted field, so an authored empty string would be a second way to say 'absent'. 1 is the smallest length that excludes it
